key_insight: The paper proposes Structure-Driven Inversion (SDI), a new paradigm that solves inverse problems by exploiting problem structure rather than iteratively minimizing an objective.
engineering_relevance: SDI could improve inversion speed, interpretability, and parameter decoupling in PDE-constrained and imaging-based engineering systems.
method: MSDI: build a pseudo-inverse in the spectral domain using unitary diagonalization.
PSDI: recover solutions through virtual-source projection in waveform inversion imaging.
PSDBP: use physical-system analogies to create three structural projections for deep neural networks.
evidence_signal: The abstract is conceptual and paradigm-setting; it does not report experimental datasets, benchmarks, or quantitative performance results.
watch_item: The main challenge is whether structure can be identified and exploited reliably across diverse inverse problems without losing robustness or generality.
paper_title: Structure-Driven Inversion: A New Paradigm for Solving Inverse Problems
